subject: Archival/DR carve-out proposal & DocuSign flow for HelixAnalytics DPA
messages:
From: Julian Price <julian.price@helixanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alyssa Cheng <alyssa.cheng@helixanalytics.com>, legal@helixanalytics.com
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA draft — question on backup/archival carve-out

Connor —

Thanks for the DPA draft. Our legal team flagged section 4.2 (Retention & Deletion) and asked for clarity around your backup/DR language. Specifically: if Helix requests deletion of customer data, how long can copies in backups/snapshots remain? They want a hard upper bound and a statement about restoration-only access by engineers.

Can you confirm how Redwood treats snapshots, whether there is a separate archival retention window, and who can access those snapshots (SRE vs. developers)?

We also want to understand whether there is an option to carve out a limited archival exemption for logs required for regulatory audits (e.g., transaction audit trails).

Appreciate a quick run-through — we are aiming to finalize next week.

Best,
Julian
VP, Security & Compliance
HelixAnalytics

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julian Price <julian.price@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA draft — question on backup/archival carve-out

Julian — thanks for the note and the quick read. Low level answers in bullet form, then proposed redline language below.

- Snapshots/backups: We retain backups for disaster recovery purposes. Backups are immutable snapshots stored separately from live customer data and are not used for analytics or product features.
- Maximum window: Standard retention for backups is 90 days; for certain regulated customers we can propose a shorter window but 90 days is our operational baseline to meet RTO/RPO targets.
- Access controls: Only designated SREs with break-glass approval and the Platform Reliability Manager (internal title: Infrastructure Lead) can restore from backups. Regular engineering teams do not have direct access to snapshot images. All restores are logged and audited.
- Archival exemption for audits: We can add a narrow carve-out that allows retention of immutable audit logs for up to 24 months if required by law, but this must be limited to specific log types and Helix must provide an audit justification.

Proposed redline (suggested language for section 4.2):
"For disaster recovery purposes only, Redwood may retain immutable backups and system snapshots containing Customer Data for a period not to exceed ninety (90) days from the date the backup was created. Access to such backups is restricted to Redwood personnel in the SRE/Platform Reliability function and requires documented break-glass authorization. Restorations from backups will be performed solely to restore Customer Data to the live environment and not for any secondary processing. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may request retention of audit log artifacts for a period up to twenty-four (24) months where retention is demonstrably required by applicable law, subject to Customer providing documented justification and Redwood's prior written consent."
I've looped in Marissa (Legal) and Karthik (Security Compliance) to validate the language and confirm whether we can operationalize a shorter backup window if needed. If that looks acceptable to you I can get a DocuSign envelope prepared — would Helix want the redline or the clean execution copy to sign?

Thanks —
Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA draft — question on backup/archival carve-out

Connor — quick legal review below. I'm okay with the substance but suggest tightening a couple of phrases to reduce ambiguity and make the carve-out auditable.

Key edits:
- Replace "may retain" with "will retain only as necessary for disaster recovery and will delete backups no later than 90 days" — this gives Helix stronger assurance.
- Add requirement that Redwood provide attestation of deletion upon request (standard template attestation).
- Narrow the audit-log carve-out to "transactional audit trails" and require Helix to specify which categories of logs at signature time.

Redlined proposal (short):
"Redwood will retain immutable backups and system snapshots containing Customer Data only as necessary for disaster recovery and will delete such backups no later than ninety (90) days from creation. Access to backups is limited to designated SRE personnel and requires documented break-glass approval; all accesses and restorations will be logged and made available to Customer on request. Customer may request retention of narrowly defined transactional audit trails for up to twenty-four (24) months where retention is required by applicable law; Customer must specify the categories of logs at the time of executing this Agreement and provide documented justification."
Operational note to Karthik: can your team confirm we can support the attestation flow (simple signed statement + deletion cert) within 10 business days of a Helix request? If not, propose an alternative SLA.

-Marissa
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA draft — question on backup/archival carve-out

Marissa/Connor — quick ops confirmation: we can do the 90-day backup retention baseline and we have break-glass controls that require two-person approval (SRE lead + on-call infra manager). Access logs are central and exportable. We can provide a deletion attestation within 10 business days, but deletions that require manual restores/verification may take longer depending on region and export checks — propose we limit the attestation SLA to confirmation that backups containing the data have been scheduled for deletion and provide the deletion token/ID once completed.

Also flagged: subprocessors list needs to be current in the DPA exhibit. I've attached the latest CSV. If Helix wants any subprocessor excluded, we'll need to evaluate alternatives or provide a justification path.

Karthik

Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: DPA draft — question on backup/archival carve-out

Julian — thanks for the questions and for the fast turnaround. Summary and proposed next steps:

1) Redline accepted in principle: Redwood will adopt the 90-day backup retention baseline with attestation on deletion and a narrowly defined audit-log carve-out (transactional audit trails only) to 24 months with justification.

2) Subprocessors: latest list attached; let us know if Helix requires any exclusions.

3) Execution: we can send a DocuSign envelope. Helix preference: sign the redline (with tracked changes) or the clean final? Connor: if they want to preserve auditability of the negotiations, we can send the redline as an attachment and a clean signature page for execution.

If Helix is okay, I'll prepare the envelope today and include: (a) the final DPA (clean), (b) a PDF of the agreed redline, (c) attestation template for deletion requests. Please reply with the preferred signer(s and emails) and whether they want the execution via DocuSign or AdobeSign.

Cheers —
